RulesSection.intro: Two teams, ten cups, one triangle. The most important rules for fair matches at a glance. You'll find all the rules on the rules page.

steps.title: Setup & first throw
steps.text: 2 vs 2. Each team has 10 cups in a triangle, with the last cup in the middle at the back. The first throw is decided by rock, paper, scissors.

steps.title: Throws
steps.text: 2 balls, 2 throws per team. Keep your elbow behind the table edge, and remember: drink first, then throw! In 1 vs 1 you throw both balls.

steps.title: Swatting
steps.text: After the ball has touched the table or a cup, it may be swatted away. Swatting too early costs a penalty cup. Distraction is allowed, but covering the cup or touching the table is not.

steps.title: Game end
steps.text: Once a team has lost all its cups, the opposing team gets a rebuttal. After a hit they keep throwing until a throw misses. If they hit all cups, the game continues with 3 new cups per team.

general.title: General rules
items: 1 vs 1: you throw both balls (2 throws per turn)

paragraphs.text: The first throw is decided by rock, paper, scissors.
The winner starts.
The throwing player's elbow must not cross the end of the table.
After repeated violations, the throw is declared invalid.
Each team uses 10 cups. The cups are always set up in a triangle.
The last cup is always placed in the middle at the back.
Distraction is generally allowed.

paragraphs.label: Allowed:
paragraphs.text: Talking, cheering, moving behind the table.

paragraphs.label: Not allowed:
paragraphs.text: Covering the cup, touching the table, standing next to the table.
If the ball lands directly in a cup, it counts as 1 cup.
Once the ball has touched a cup, it may be swatted away.
If the ball is deliberately bounced off the table and then lands in a cup, it counts as 2 cups.
After the ball has touched the table, it may be swatted away immediately.
If a thrown ball comes back over your half of the table, the throwing team can get it back (a “recover”). The opposing team may swat it away! The ball must not touch the floor!
A special throw (under difficult conditions) can be counted as a trick shot – after agreeing with the referee.
If both players of a team score in the same turn, the team gets 2 additional throws.
If both players hit the same cup, 1 additional cup of the throwing team's choice has to be drunk.
After the ball has touched the table or a cup, it may be swatted away.
Swatting too early = penalty cup.
A ball may be swatted out of a cup if it is visibly spinning inside the cup. A cup only counts as hit if the ball stays in the cup.
If a ball is thrown at a cup that already contains a ball, that ball may not be swatted away.
Once a team has lost all its cups, the opposing team gets the chance to throw again (rebuttal).

paragraphs.label: With 3 or more cups:
paragraphs.text: Both players may throw.

paragraphs.label: With 2 or fewer cups:
paragraphs.text: Only one player may throw.
After a hit, the team may keep throwing until a throw misses. If the team hits all cups, 3 new cups per team are set up. The game continues.

fairplay: Disputes are settled by a referee.
Unsportsmanlike behavior can be punished with penalty cups or loss of throws.

SkillRating.ratingVerlaufDerLetzten: Rating trend of the last {count} matches, currently {v} points
SkillRating.deinRatingIstEine: Your rating is a number from 0 to 1000. You start at {START_RATING}. After every match the value goes up or down, depending on how the match turned out compared with what was expected.
SkillRating.ausDenRatingsBeider: The ratings of both teams determine who goes into the match as the favorite (in 2 vs 2 the team average counts). A win against a stronger opponent earns many points, a win against a clearly weaker one hardly any. Conversely, losing to a weaker opponent costs more.
SkillRating.zumErgebnisZaehltDer: The result counts the win (70 %) and the share of cups your team hit (30 %). A 10:2 is therefore worth more than a 10:9, and a narrow loss costs less than a clear one.
SkillRating.inDenErstenMatches: In the first matches the rating fluctuates more so it quickly finds your level. The steps get smaller with every match. A single match can change it by at most ±{MAX_DELTA} points.
SkillRating.dieTrefferquoteGehtNicht: Hit rate is not part of it. Someone who hits well in just a few matches therefore doesn't land on top right away. Until match {PROVISIONAL_MATCHES} your rating counts as provisional, and you enter the ranking after {MIN_RANKED_MATCHES} matches.
SkillRating.wieBeiDeinenStatistiken: As with your statistics: only matches against registered opponents, and only matches after your last statistics reset. The time range filter does not apply to the rating.
